title: Soft-continuation SSE: semantic sentinels + ack-offset reconnection protocol for functioncall atomicity
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Summary:
Implement a "soft-continuation" extension to our SSE streaming protocol that makes reconnects safe for structured outputs and function/tool calls without requiring full event replays or large resume tokens. The goal is atomicity for functioncall frames and structured JSON outputs while minimizing bytes re-sent and avoiding duplicate function invocations in downstream tool chains.

Key ideas:
- Ack-offset: clients periodically ACK the last byte-offset they consumed for a stream (simple integer). On reconnect the client supplies last_seen_offset. The server will only re-send from a negotiated rewind window (configurable) if the offset falls inside a recoverable buffer.
- Semantic sentinels: in addition to offsets, the server emits small "semantic sentinel" markers at logical safepoints (function-call boundaries, top-level JSON object boundaries, or explicit user-defined checkpoints). Sentinels are short text tokens that are idempotent markers for reconnection semantics (eg. "@@SENTINEL:FC-42:END@@").
- Chunk integrity: each SSE chunk carries a lightweight 32-bit rolling hash (not cryptographic) and a short chunk id (merkle-style prefix). On reconnect, client and server reconcile by comparing the last acknowledged chunk id/hash before re-sending to avoid partial-chunk duplication or truncation.
- Handshake negotiation: new SSE header X-SSE-SoftCont: 1 indicates both sides support the extension; accompanying header X-SSE-Sentinel-Granularity: {char,object,function} negotiates sentinel semantics.
- Functioncall atomicity: function call frames (structured function call events) are only acknowledged at function boundary sentinels. Clients that reconnect will not see duplicate function invocations because the server will detect the last confirmed sentinel and only re-emit frames after that marker.
- Backpressure hints & pacing: include per-chunk "consumption-rate" hint field so server can tune micro-batching; helps ensure replay window remains small under heavy load.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Why not large resume tokens? Resume tokens store opaque transcript state which is costly to persist per-client in hosted mode. Ack-offset + sentinel approach is lightweight and compatible with proxying (CDN/edge) setups.
- Why use rolling hashes instead of full checksums? We want a small footprint that catches common truncation/duplication cases but keeps CPU minimal. Critical security-sensitive endpoints can opt-in to stronger signatures via separate headers.
- Complexity: requires moderate changes to runner and gateway. We must ensure private/dedicated customers can toggle granularity and rewind-window sizes.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
- Server emits sentinel markers for functioncall completion and top-level JSON boundaries in 99% of responses for supported models.
- Reconnect test harness can resume from a last_seen_offset and receive a stream where no functioncall is duplicated and structured JSON remains parseable.
- End-to-end tests for proxies (nginx/edge) show reconnection success with ack-offset negotiation intact.
- Latency overhead < 2% p95 token latency when sentinels and hashes enabled.

Rollout plan:
1) RFC + conformance test harness (internal): implement server-side sentinel emission in dev branch; provide a thin-reference client that demonstrates reconnection flows.
2) Canary in Dedicated region only with X-SSE-SoftCont header opt-in. Monitor functioncall duplication and error rates for 2 weeks.
3) Enable for hosted API behind feature flag; allow customers to opt-in per-key.
4) Default-on when we validate that duplication rates and latency budgets meet SLO.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- New metrics: sentinel_emit_rate, ack_offset_reconcile_count, reconnect_replay_bytes, functioncall_duplicate_rate.
- Alert if functioncall_duplicate_rate > 0.1% over 6h on canary.

Security/privacy considerations:
- Sentinels do not contain customer data; they are opaque tokens mapped to internal safepoints.
- Because ack-offset exposes only byte positions, it should be safe for multi-tenant gateways; but avoid using offsets for any customer-identifiable mapping in logs.

Implementation tasks (high-level):
- Runtime: small encoder change to inject sentinel events and append chunk metadata (hash, chunk id).
- Gateway: parse X-SSE-SoftCont headers, maintain short replay buffer per connection (configurable size), reconcile on reconnect.
- Client SDKs: add opt-in reconnection logic that sends last_seen_offset and last_seen_chunk_id; expose API to opt into stronger sentinel semantics.
- Tests: unit for chunk hash logic, integration for reconnection with proxies, fuzz for partial-chunk corruption handling.

Notes on compatibility with function/tool calling: the sentinel at function boundary is the source of truth for whether a remote tool should be invoked again. Tool clients must record the last confirmed sentinel id alongside any side-effects; this makes deduplication feasible for idempotent/non-idempotent tools when paired with customer-side guards.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Server emits sentinels at function and JSON boundaries for most supported output flows. 2) Reconnect from last_seen_offset replay only re-emits events after last confirmed sentinel; no duplicate function invocation observed in integration runs. 3) Canary latency overhead < 2% p95. 4) Telemetry for functioncall_duplicate_rate <= 0.1% during canary.
